two_criteria.shipped_any_epsilon: independent evaluator stale_hops prediction moves up by more than 1e-10 (same tolerance closed.py uses when it writes independent_stale_increase)
two_criteria.problem_statement_threshold: defect = over-threshold item; count source beers below the sensory detection threshold that crossed above it

note: Two readings, both reported, neither sufficient on its own. (a) Problem-statement reading (defects are over-threshold items): among source beers that started below the sensory detection threshold, the count that crossed above it is Unconstrained 7, PointConstraint 0, UncertaintyConstraint 0 out of 23 testable rows; the Reject policy returns the source spectrum unchanged and therefore crosses 0. (b) Strict any-epsilon reading (any upward move above 1e-10 counts): Unconstrained 6/9, PointConstraint 5/9, UncertaintyConstraint 4/9, Reject 0/9. The two readings differ by at most ~0.05 points on the 0-6 scale, which is well inside the model's own ~0.23 MAE on stale_hops, so neither can support a guarantee of non-worsening and neither can be used to dismiss the constraint as ineffective. The Reject row is an internal consistency check: its stale_change is exactly zero up to float round-off (largest magnitude 5.6e-17), so it must read 0 under both readings. stale_hops has no usable chemical threshold (it is a sensory proxy) and so cannot enter the threshold-crossing count at all.
